title: Token-conditioned Mirror ReFT
hypothesis: For continuous token contexts, a rank-4 LoReFT intervention with a small context-generated Givens View recovers tokenwise interventions with fewer serialized bytes than FiLM and generic coordinate MLP while preserving quality.
physical_object: Fixed shared synthetic 64x4 representation-intervention basis and shared token projection
mirror_coordinate: Two context-generated Givens angles per token, applied to a projected rank-4 activation code
controls: Linear LoReFT coefficients from concatenated hidden/context inputs
Generic MLP producing rank-4 LoReFT coefficients

task.context_distribution: Continuous iid Gaussian; test examples use unseen context vectors

development.selection: Select learning rate by mean validation intervention NRMSE across all methods.

paid_objects: generic coefficient MLP or direct coefficient generator
all inference metadata and serialization state

success_gate: Every fresh world has intervention NRMSE <=0.05; Mirror payload <=80% FiLM bytes; and Mirror relative NRMSE is within 10% of generic MLP LoReFT.
failure_gate: Quality/storage fails or a simpler control matches quality at equal/fewer bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic continuous-context intervention only; Givens-aligned teacher.
No pretrained Transformer, language, capacity, or natural-token claim.
Continuous test contexts do not establish compositional task capacity.
